newsitem.title: LATVIA: GRINDEX EYES BOURSE OFFICIAL LIST.
newsitem.headline: GRINDEX EYES BOURSE OFFICIAL LIST.

text.p: Grindex, the pharmaceutical firm in the final stages of privatisation, said on Monday it plans to apply to enter the stock exchange official list early next year.
"I expect Grindex to get a bourse listing early in 1998 or late this year," manager Valdis Jekabsons told Reuters.
"Given the good price that our new share issue of 1.55 million shares fetched, Grindex might as well aim for the bourse's official list," Jekabsons said.
Grindex had a new issue of 1.55 million shares, aimed at attracting foreign capital in the second stage of its sell-off, auctioned off to Estonian company Arials on July 19.
Arials is to pay 3.09 million lats for its stake in Grindex.

"The money that the auction brought in more than covers our three-year business development plan worked out with Coopers & Lybrand," Jekabsons said, noting the firm's products would be brought up to European Union standards.
Arials will have to pay for the stake in three months and the funds will remain with Grindex as investment.
"Another 25 percent of the state-owned stake of 4.4 million shares will be offered to the owner of the new issue," Jekabsons said. "That would basically complete Grindex's privatisation."
"Somewhere in September or October 18 percent of our stake will be offered to employees," Jekabsons said. "They will pay 60 percent in vouchers and 40 percent in cash."
"This money, however, will be paid into the privatisation agency coffers," Jekabsons said.

The restructuring programme of the state-owned Savings Bank (Krajbanka) will receive get five percent of the shares, the management five percent and four percent will go to the inventors of Grindex products.
"With the new issue, our share capital now reaches 5.9 million lats," Jekabsons said.
